<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**11** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **12** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e8a78c4bdf0ec079cdb56e6e6c6f32d6f4ac8e42` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `ef691dd87ec57f7eba1edd4b36bc4f714a24c212` — the merge of head `36a9089a809745c2a0e02ee245a643ae73db07c8` into base `e8a78c4bdf0ec079cdb56e6e6c6f32d6f4ac8e42`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin ef691dd87ec57f7eba1edd4b36bc4f714a24c212 && git checkout ef691dd87ec57f7eba1edd4b36bc4f714a24c212
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin e8a78c4bdf0ec079cdb56e6e6c6f32d6f4ac8e42 36a9089a809745c2a0e02ee245a643ae73db07c8 && git checkout -B drift-repro e8a78c4bdf0ec079cdb56e6e6c6f32d6f4ac8e42 && git merge --no-ff 36a9089a809745c2a0e02ee245a643ae73db07c8

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e8a78c4bdf0ec079cdb56e6e6c6f32d6f4ac8e42
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## L2 round on head 60d4e1c6c7: finding S1 sent back · 2026-11-17T22:46Z

The seat's at-tier reviewer sub-agent read this head and found no must-fix, one should-fix, and three nits. Its record is NOT posted as the record of this head: `verify-review-tier.mjs` refused its transcript, because one turn is a synthetic usage-limit error turn (every model turn is CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER). The rule is a fresh at-tier run, never a renamed tier. S1 moves the head anyway, so the fresh record is rendered on the fixed head.

**S1 (should-fix).** The record-root date-text pass stands down on any operator fault of the roots' Timestamp typing (`recordRootReadsFaultTimestampTyping` matches `UNSOUND_OVERLOAD_RE`), not only on the date-arith shape it defers to. So, read from the tree and the cel-js 8.0.0 checker (not run):
- (a) `record.due_date - record.borrow_date GT 3` gives 0 findings, while the bare spelling is refused (`date-text-arithmetic-run-fails`, the registered `formula-date-subtraction-refused` shape).
- (b) `record.due_date GE "2026-01-01" && timestamp(record.borrow_date) LT now()` gives 0 findings, but is refused with the conjuncts swapped, so the answer depends on operand order. The bare spelling is refused in both orders.
Fix sent to the dev: route (i), stand down only where the roots' Timestamp-typing fault is date-arith. Pin (a), and (b) in both orders, and keep the `record.due_date + 1` control.

Nits sent along: N1, one shared constant for the root-read gate (`RECORD_ROOT_READ_RE`) and `firstTypeMismatch`'s inline one. N2, `firstTypeMismatch`'s comment "The date verdicts stay the bare name's alone" is now true of date-arith only. N3, a `-run-may-fail` root-read pin at the lint or door layer is optional.
Also noted by the reviewer, for a follow-up card: the index spelling `timestamp(record['borrow_date'])` reaches neither pass.
